official.deadline_note: Scholarship consideration requires applying by 15 January (summer admission) or 15 September (winter admission); EU/EEA/Swiss applicants apply by 1 March (summer) / 15 October (winter) but cannot obtain this scholarship. Three named Master's programmes (Journalism, Media and Globalisation; Neuroscience and Neuroimaging; Soils and Global Change) have special application deadlines. Final acceptance deadline for summer-admission offers is 1 April (1 November for winter admission); Science/Technology tuition-waiver awards continue to be made until that date.
official.application_cycle: Summer intake with start of studies August/September 2027 (academic year 2027/2028) - application round opens 1 November and closes 15 January for non-EU applicants; winter intake with start January/February has a 15 September deadline
official.status_note: Standing scheme considered in every admission round; the page lists the scholarship as an active, state-funded programme. The summer application round opens 1 November 2026 (non-EU deadline 15 January 2027); the winter round closed on 15 September 2026. Official page last revised 8 July 2026.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship is a tuition fee waiver - in some cases full, in some cases partial. At the Faculty of Natural Sciences and the Faculty of Technical Sciences the awards are 100% tuition fee waivers. The waiver covers tuition fees only; books and other course material are not covered.
benefits: In some cases, the scholarship is a full or partly tuition waiver.

Faculty of Arts: Tuition fee waiver + monthly grant towards living expenses.
Aarhus BSS: Tuition fee waiver + monthly grant towards living expenses.
Faculty of Natural Sciences: Tuition fee waiver.
Faculty of Technical Sciences: Tuition fee waiver.
At some faculties that offer only tuition waivers, the faculty may offer other relevant services, e.g. assistance in searching for a relevant student job.
eligibility: Scholarships can only be awarded to applicants who are liable to pay tuition fees.

official.application_route: Submit the online Master's admission application by 15 January (summer) or 15 September (winter); AU automatically assesses the same application for the Danish State Scholarship - there is no separate application form.
official.citizenship_residency: Scholarships can only be awarded to applicants who are liable to pay tuition fees - i.e. applicants from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland (including holders of a British national overseas passport) who are not exempt; EU/EEA/Swiss citizens cannot apply.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scheme is specifically for non-EU/EEA/Swiss international applicants; EU/EEA/Swiss students cannot apply for scholarships at AU.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No subject restriction for eligibility, but the form of the award differs by faculty (Arts and Aarhus BSS include a monthly living grant; Natural Sciences and Technical Sciences offer tuition waivers only), and at some faculties strategic focus may be placed on selected degree programmes or applicants from specific countries.
official.duration: Tuition waiver for the duration of the Master's degree programme; the monthly grant is 'typically but not always for the duration of your Master's degree programme'.
official.description: Aarhus University offers a limited number of Danish state scholarships for non-EU students, financed solely by the Danish state, to the most talented applicants. When you apply for admission, the university automatically considers you for a Danish State Scholarship - no separate application is required. The award is a full or partial tuition fee waiver, which at some faculties is combined with a monthly grant towards living expenses.
official.program_type: Danish state scholarship for non-EU students - Master's level tuition fee waiver (with monthly living grant at some faculties)
official.english_requirement: Proficiency comparable to the Danish upper secondary course 'English B level', documented by IELTS Academic 6.5 (minimum 6 in each subscore), TOEFL iBT 83 (minimum 20 per subscore) for results achieved before 21 January 2026 or 4.5 (minimum 4.0 per subscore) for results achieved after 21 January 2026, or Cambridge English Qualifications (180 points on the Cambridge English Scale; C2 Proficiency minimum 190 points). Tests must not be more than two years old on the day the application portal opens. Exemptions include completed Bachelor's or Master's degrees taught in English from universities in Australia, Canada, New Zealand, the UK, the USA or Ireland, and degrees from Danish institutions. Documentation must be submitted by the application deadline (15 January for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens starting in August/September).

verification.notes: All scheme facts taken directly from Aarhus University's own masters.au.dk pages (scholarships page revised 8 July 2026): automatic consideration, faculty-by-faculty waiver/grant types, 15 January / 15 September deadlines, and selection process. No monetary figure for the tuition waiver or the monthly grant is published on any official AU page, so amount, currency and period stay null; living-cost coverage varies by faculty and is therefore not recorded as a blanket value. The previously catalogued URL (international.au.dk/education/finance/scholarships) now 404s; the current official pages are under masters.au.dk.

applicant_utility.summary: This award is not something you apply for separately: AU screens every fee-liable Master's applicant for the Danish State Scholarship as part of the admission file, so your only real control point is filing the admission application by 15 January (summer start) or 15 September (winter start). What you get varies by faculty - Arts and Aarhus BSS pair a tuition waiver with a monthly living grant, while Natural Sciences and Technical Sciences give waiver-only support. Selection is academic-first, with priority for excellent qualifications and typically only one or two awards per programme, and the decision arrives with your admission letter on a very short acceptance clock. Treat it as a bonus that reduces an already-funded budget, not as guaranteed funding for your studies in Denmark.
applicant_utility.best_fit: High-achieving non-EU applicants with strong transcripts who are targeting Faculty of Arts or Aarhus BSS programmes (where a monthly living grant exists) and who can cover remaining living costs from savings or external loans even if only a waiver lands.
application_readiness_checklist: File the Master's admission application in AU's online portal well before 15 January for a summer start - scholarship consideration ends on that date regardless of admission outcomes.
Pay the 150 EUR application fee (covers up to three AU applications) and upload the receipt to every application so the file is processed by the deadline.

Have an accepted English qualification ready and uploaded by the same deadline - IELTS Academic 6.5 (6.0 per band), the applicable TOEFL iBT scale, or Cambridge 180 - and check the two-year validity window against the day the portal opens.

Keep the admission file itself complete (transcripts, degree documentation, CV/motivation as the programme requires) since scholarship scoring rides entirely on it; upload nothing extra for the scholarship.
Plan a fallback budget for Denmark before results arrive - housing deposit, furniture, bicycle or bus card and first-month costs - in case the award is waiver-only or does not materialise.
common_rejection_risks: Applying after 15 January (summer) or 15 September (winter): late applicants are excluded from scholarship consideration even if admitted.

A mediocre academic file relative to the applicant pool - assessment happens among academically qualified applicants with priority for excellent grades, so strong admission performance may still yield a fee invoice instead of an award.

Faculty mismatch: identical profiles can receive waiver-plus-grant (Arts, BSS) or waiver-only (Natural Sciences, Technical Sciences), and some faculties weight specific programmes or countries strategically.
Assuming EU rules protect you: EU/EEA/Swiss citizens cannot apply, and non-EU passport holders with EU residence can still be tuition-liable.
Later waiver rounds through March can be missed if you decline your admission offer before the final deadline (1 April summer / 1 November winter) out of funding anxiety.
Letting the scholarship-offer acceptance window lapse - AU states it is very short.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: For waiver-only awards (and any partial case) the entire cost of living sits with you: AU states the scholarship may not cover all living expenses and advises supplementing with savings, a home-country student loan or a student job, listing room deposit, furniture and transport among settling-in costs. Books and course materials are not covered in any award type, AU provides no further financial assistance, and the monthly grant (where it exists) is taxed in Denmark unless you hold a tax exemption as a student from a designated developing country.
document_audit: Do not upload scholarship-specific documents - AU explicitly says no additional documentation is needed, so extra files add nothing and can only confuse the file.
The English test result must sit inside the admission application by the deadline, not be sent separately afterwards.
The application-fee receipt must be attached to each application individually, not just one.
Keep the eventual scholarship offer letter: it is needed to obtain a Danish tax card, without which 55% of each monthly grant payment is withheld as tax until the card is issued.
If you receive a waiver without a monthly grant, you must separately document sufficient funds to SIRI for the student residence permit - this proof requirement catches many waiver-only recipients.
alerts: The 15 January / 15 September application cut-off is also the scholarship cut-off: the later 1 March or 15 October deadlines are EU-applicant routes that come with no scholarship possibility.
The award is non-transferable - it is tied to the exact Master's programme in your offer and cannot be moved to another AU programme.
If funding is decisive for your decision, do not decline an admission offer before 1 April (summer) or 1 November (winter); late waiver offers keep arriving until then.

Monthly grants only start after you land: you need a CPR number, a NemKonto (Danish Easy Account) and a Danish tax card, and the first payment appears in September/October (summer start) or February/March (winter start) at the earliest.
EU/EEA/Swiss applicants are outright ineligible, so applicants who recently acquired EU residency should check the exemptions page rather than assume either outcome.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: One submission covers both admission and scholarship: upload the online Master's application (with fee receipt and English documentation) by 15 January or 15 September, and AU's academic and scholarship assessments run together, with any waiver or grant delivered inside the admission letter in the application system.
